messages.author: 92555aa28f92a6ba
messages.subject: Seize and release encapsulation
parts:
Hello,

Let's say I have three hospital wards, with three types of beds.  Two of the wards feed in to the other A->C B->C. A bed cannot be released in A or B until a bed in C is available. Wards A and B also have branches to other wards. I could write out the full trajectories for each branch from A and B but in my work I have a large schematic with multiple wards and branches so I'd like to encapsulate each ward. Is there a way of attaching something like a flag to the branch A->C that can tell C it came from A? 

Hope this is enough explanation. Let me know if you need a small example. Help would be hugely appreciated!

Kind regards,

Andre

Option 1: if you feed A and B from different generators, they'll have
different prefixes, and you can get an arrival's name with get_name.

Option 2: you can set an attribute that can be retrieved with get_attribute.

messages.author: c9573d5f110a3778
messages.subject: Seize and release encapsulation
parts:
Hi Andre or Inaki,

How do you code the dependency between ward C's availability and the seize timeout I'm A or B? I have a similar circumstance in my retail store simulation... I have set one specific timeout based upon a probability distribution, but I don't want the seizure to complete until the next resource is available, and I don't want the object in the trajectory to leave the system.

Thanks
Ralph

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Seize and release encapsulation
parts:
2018-04-09 12:57 GMT+02:00 Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com>:
> Hi Andre or Inaki,
>
> How do you code the dependency between ward C's availability and the seize timeout I'm A or B? I have a similar circumstance in my retail store simulation... I have set one specific timeout based upon a probability distribution, but I don't want the seizure to complete until the next resource is available, and I don't want the object in the trajectory to leave the system.

You can do something like the following:

- seize A
- timeout based on some distribution
- branch, if C is not available (queue is full)
- wait until a signal is received from an arrival releasing C
- release A
- seize C

simmer.bricks has a wait_until verb, which is a shortcut for trap >
wait > untrap.

Iñaki

>
> Thanks
> Ralph
>

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Seize and release encapsulation
parts:
Do you have a vignette on how you may use wait_until?  I'm going to reprofile my trajectory to use visit() instead of seize-->timeout-->release, so I may as well try wait_until as well.

I want to have a customer's purchase (the arrival) waiting in a storage space, with a timeout determined by a distribution.  At the end of the timeout, a worker will then be seized to retrieve the purchase from the storage space, unless the worker is currently seized by a different arrival.  In that case, then the purchase will stay in storage until the worker is available.

Ralph

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Seize and release encapsulation
parts:
2018-04-09 19:46 GMT+02:00 Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com>:
> Do you have a vignette on how you may use wait_until?

See the examples: https://r-simmer.org/extensions/bricks/reference/wait_n.html

What is not specified there is that you must use "send" in another
point of your simulation to trigger the signal.

> I'm going to
> reprofile my trajectory to use visit() instead of seize-->timeout-->release,
> so I may as well try wait_until as well.

Please note that all the functions in simmer.bricks are shortcuts. You
may write "visit", but the trajectory will still consist of a
seize>timeout>release sequence. That is, you must keep this in mind in
case you are using rollbacks.

In the same way, wait_until is equivalent to trap>wait>untrap for a
single input signal (more 'wait' are added if several signals are
provided). The helpl page for each function clearly explains this
equivalence and contains several examples.

> I want to have a customer's purchase (the arrival) waiting in a storage
> space, with a timeout determined by a distribution. At the end of the
> timeout, a worker will then be seized to retrieve the purchase from the
> storage space, unless the worker is currently seized by a different arrival.
> In that case, then the purchase will stay in storage until the worker is
> available.

Then your use case is different from the other thread (i.e., "Build up
a finite queue without rejecting arrivals"). You said: "I don't want
the seizure to complete until the next resource is available". And for
"availability", I understood "if I seize the next finite-queue
resource I won't get dropped", which is the case in the other thread.

In your case, you don't want to release the storage until you can
actually "use" the worker. So the interleaved seize/release pattern
described by Mark is exactly what you are looking for:

- seize storage area
- timeout
- seize worker
- release storage area

Iñaki

> Ralph
